Documents:
Document 1: The Private Secretary The Private Secretary is a 1883 farce in three acts, by Charles Hawtrey. The play, adapted from a German original, depicts the vicissitudes of a mild young clergyman, innocently caught up in the machinations of two irresponsible young men who are bent on escaping their creditors. When the play opened in London the notices for the piece were hostile, and it was seen as a stop-gap in the schedule of the theatrical company presenting it. Document 2: The Private Secretary (1935 film) The Private Secretary is a 1935 British comedy film directed by Henry Edwards and starring Edward Everett Horton, Barry MacKay, Judy Gunn and Oscar Asche. It is an adaptation of the play "The Private Secretary" by Charles Henry Hawtrey. It was made at Twickenham Studios. Wealthy Englishman Robert Cattermole returns from a trip to India to discover that instead of achieving success, his beloved nephew Robert has got into such debt that he now disguises himself as a mild-mannered minister to evade his creditors. Look for a sentence in the documents which shows that the answers do not conflict, because
- they refer to different senses: different events, editions, versions, conditions, places or measures (an original release and a re-release, for example), or
- they refer to different times: the value changed, and each answer was right at its own date.
Use only what the documents say: nothing you know from elsewhere, and no explanation of your own. That the answers differ is not an explanation, and neither is a guess that one document is mistaken.

Reply with JSON only. If a sentence explains the difference:
{"explained": true, "by": "sense", "document": 1, "quote": "", "labels": {"A": "", "B": ""}}
"by" is "sense" or "time". "quote" is that sentence, copied word for word, and "document" is the number of the document it is in. "labels" gives, for each answer, the sense or the date it refers to.
If no sentence explains it:
{"explained": false}

Inside a JSON string, write a double quote as \".
